title: Widows
lead: In the ancient world a widow, especially one without sons, often had no income, no protector and no legal voice. The Bible names widows again and again among those God defends (Exodus 22:22–24; Psalm 68:5) and commands his people to care for them (Deuteronomy 24:17–22; James 1:27).

sections.b: The Law warns, "Never treat a widow or a fatherless child harshly" (Exodus 22:22–24) and calls God "a defender of widows" (Psalm 68:5). Elijah is sent to a starving widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:8–24), and Elisha rescues a widow's sons from debt slavery (2 Kings 4:1–7). The prophets judge Israel by its treatment of widows (Isaiah 1:17, 23). Jesus raises a widow's only son at Nain (Luke 7:11–17) and praises a poor widow's two coins (Luke 21:1–4). The early church organized care for widows (Acts 6:1; 1 Timothy 5:3–16), and James calls caring for widows and orphans pure religion (James 1:27).
